learningObjective: Explain why def-use chains are trivial to compute in SSA compared to non-SSA IR.

canonicalClaims.claim: In SSA form, each variable name has exactly one textual definition, so each use trivially points to a unique def; no reaching-definitions dataflow analysis is required to build def-use chains.
conditions: The IR is in valid SSA form (each name defined exactly once).
Phi-functions merge reaching definitions at joins.
nonImplications: Does not imply that def-use chain construction is free; a linear scan is still needed.
Does not imply non-SSA IRs cannot compute def-use chains; they simply require reaching-definitions analysis first.

misconceptions.claim: SSA prohibits loops so def-use chains cannot cross backedges.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SSA supports loops via loop-header phis; def-use chains cross backedges through phi operands.

misconceptions.claim: SSA merges phi values into a single memory slot at runtime.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Phis are IR pseudo-instructions eliminated during out-of-SSA to copies at predecessor blocks; they do not correspond to a runtime memory slot.

misconceptions.claim: SSA guarantees every use is reachable from every def.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SSA guarantees each use has a unique reaching def, not that all defs reach all uses.

implementationFacts: In LLVM, llvm::Value::use_iterator provides the def-use chain in O(1) navigation per use.
SSA def-use chains support fast constant propagation, SCCP, dead-code elimination.
performanceScenarios: SSA-based dataflow analyses (SCCP, GVN) leverage sparse def-use chains for scalable analysis.
